text:
Eeli Tolvanen had nine points in five games at the 2018 Olympics as a teenager, and he has spent the years since trying to become the scorer that tournament promised. With the Rangers he's a third-line winger beside Will Cuylle, playing about 12 and a half minutes a night, with six points in 18 games.

The goals are coming more easily than the chances. He has four on 3.2 expected and a 20% shooting percentage that won't hold, and the Rangers have scored about five more goals than expected with him on the ice. Strip that away and the five-on-five picture is weak: about six points of expected goal share worse with him on than off. Evolving-Hockey's numbers last season in Seattle said offense wasn't really his game, though his teammates there were about as weak as it gets by impact.

He did snap a slump with a two-point night against St. Louis, including an empty-net goal. His shot is still a weapon, harder than 89% of the league by NHL Edge. Our range has him at 10 to 19 goals over a full season. Useful depth, as long as nobody expects the Olympic version.
headline: Tolvanen, still a shooter
